package.name: typesafe
package.packageFile:
# TYPESAFE, fully declarative.
#
# One vendor endpoint, POST /v1/systemone, answers typed questions about a piece of state:
# pick an option, place on a scale, or say whether a statement holds. The answer is a value
# and a probability distribution, never prose, so a workflow branches on it directly.
#
# Four nodes over the one call: three ask a single question of one type, and the fourth
# sends a whole map of questions in one round trip, which is how the vendor is meant to be
# used when several judgements share the same state.

name: typesafe
displayName: TypeSafe
description: Typed decisions from Jev, TypeSafe's System One model; a value and a probability, never prose
version: 1.0.0
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1789700088/gravity/icons/typesafe_ai_logo.jpg

features:
  - Choose one option from a described list, with a probability for each
  - Score state on an ordered scale of described levels
  - Answer whether a statement is true, as a probability
  - Ask several questions of one state in a single call

allowedHosts:
  - api.typesafe.ai

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]

credentials.typesafeCredential.yaml:
name: typesafeCredential
displayName: TypeSafe
description: Credentials for the TypeSafe API
documentationUrl: https://console.typesafe.ai/settings/keys

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your TypeSafe API key
    placeholder: ts-

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.

- emit: score
  from: response
  value: "return response.answers.answer.score"

# The vendor's own advice for combining scales of different lengths: divide by the top index.
- emit: normalized
  from: response
  value: >-
    return (Object.keys(response.answers.answer.legend || {}).length > 1)
      ? response.answers.answer.score / (Object.keys(response.answers.answer.legend).length - 1)
      : response.answers.answer.score

- emit: probabilities
  from: response
  value: "return response.answers.answer.probabilities || {}"

- emit: confidence
  from: response
  value: "return response.answers.answer.confidence"

- emit: legend
  from: response
  value: "return response.answers.answer.legend || {}"

- emit: usage
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      model: response.model,
      inputTokens: (response.usage || {}).input_tokens || 0,
      outputTokens: (response.usage || {}).output_tokens || 0
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# One synchronous call. Every question type goes through the same endpoint; this node sends
# exactly one, keyed `answer`, so the reply is read at a fixed path.
#
# STATE MAY BE STRUCTURE. The field is a string so it can be typed or templated, but the
# vendor reads a JSON object or array as named fields rather than as prose, so a value that
# is a whole JSON document is parsed before it is sent. Prose stays prose.

- name: ask
  method: POST
  url: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.typesafeCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 60000
  # 529 is the vendor's own overloaded code, alongside the usual rate limit and server errors.
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529]

  body:
    model: "return config.model || 'jev-latest'"
    state: >-
      return (typeof config.state === 'string'
        && ((config.state.trim().startsWith('{') && config.state.trim().endsWith('}'))
          || (config.state.trim().startsWith('[') && config.state.trim().endsWith(']'))))
        ? JSON.parse(config.state)
        : config.state
    questions: >-
      return {
        answer: {
          type: 'score',
          instructions: config.instructions,
          criteria: Array.isArray(config.levels) ? config.levels : [config.levels]
        }
      }

  error:
    # A reply without the one answer asked for is a failure whatever the status was.
    when: "return !((response.answers || {}).answer)"
    message: >-
      return 'TypeSafe returned no answer.'
        + (response.error ? ' ' + JSON.stringify(response.error) : '')
        + (response.detail ? ' ' + JSON.stringify(response.detail) : '')
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [state, instructions, levels]
  properties:
    state:
      type: string
      title: State
      description: >-
        What to judge: a message, a passage, a record. Text is sent as text; a JSON object or
        array (for example {{ toJSON signal.x }}) is sent as structure, which the model reads
        better than prose when the data has named fields.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai":
        editable: true
    instructions:
      type: string
      title: Instructions
      description: The quality to rate, as a question. Shared blocks work here.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai":
        editable: true
    levels:
      type: array
      title: Levels
      description: >-
        Two to ten level descriptions as a JSON list, lowest first. Describe each as a
        concrete situation rather than a relative word like "worse".
      default: []
      "ui:field": template
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: jev-latest is the stable release; jev-preview is the newest build.
      enum: [jev-latest, jev-preview]
      default: jev-latest
"ui:order": [state, instructions, levels, model]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: score
    type: number
    description: Position on the scale
  - name: normalized
    type: number
    description: The score as 0 to 1
  - name: probabilities
    type: object
    description: Each level's probability
  - name: confidence
    type: number
    description: 0 to 1, how clear the level is
  - name: legend
    type: object
    description: Level index to its description
  - name: usage
    type: object
    description: model, inputTokens, outputTokens

credentials:
  - name: typesafeCredential
    required: true
    displayName: TypeSafe
files.node.yaml:
type: TypeSafeScore
# One call, one reply: the endpoint answers synchronously.
kind: PromiseNode

name: TypeSafe Score
category: AI
color: "#1D4ED8"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1789700088/gravity/icons/typesafe_ai_logo.jpg

description: Place state on an ordered scale of described levels, with a probability per level

whenToUse: >-
  Rate a piece of text or data on one quality with a graded answer: how severe a bug report
  is, how satisfied a customer sounds, how well a candidate fits, how urgent a request is.
  The levels are described in order from low to high and the answer is a position on that
  scale plus a probability for every level, so a threshold or a sort can act on it without
  parsing prose. Right when the options are ordered steps of one thing; unordered
  categories are a choice, and one quality with no steps is a statement to test.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (who-can-run-it.md). Compulsory on every node, so that a node nobody
# thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A pure read: the same state and levels give the same distribution, and nothing is
  # written anywhere.
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
# Asserts the SHAPE, not the verdict: the score lies on the three-level scale, the
# normalized score is a fraction, and the legend echoes three levels.

testData:
  config:
    state: "Checkout fails with a 500 on every attempt since this morning; nobody can buy."
    instructions: How severe is this bug report?
    levels:
      - Cosmetic; no impact to functionality
      - A feature is broken or degraded, but a workaround exists
      - Blocking; no workaround exists
    model: jev-latest
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    score: "return output.score >= 0 && output.score <= 2"
    normalized: "return output.normalized >= 0 && output.normalized <= 1"
    probabilities: >-
      return Object.keys(output.probabilities).length === 3
        && Math.abs(Object.values(output.probabilities).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) - 1) < 0.01
    confidence: "return output.confidence >= 0 && output.confidence <= 1"
    legend: "return Object.keys(output.legend).length === 3"
    usage: "return output.usage.inputTokens > 0 && typeof output.usage.model === 'string'"
